correctness.rationale: Explicit exponential formulas yield trPhi=e^(sigma t)g(t)+e^(mu t)h(t), D=e^(2(a-d)t); the quadratic Jury criterion reduces stability to |trPhi|<1+D. In the stated parameter wedge, kappa>d-a>0, hence sigma>0, while mu<0. Uniform simple zeros of g(t)=R cos(omega t-theta) localize all late stable times; |H'| dominates |D'| in fixed small zero-neighborhoods, so the two Jury crossings bound a unique component. Uniform scaled Taylor expansions yield boundary displacement exp(-sigma*t_n)/(omega R); geometric domination yields the exact tail measure. Independent SciPy exponentials agreed with derived trace and showed stable centers at (a,d)=(0.1,11), (0.4,3). This verifies the claimed reduced ODE; finite checks do not establish the asymptotic theorem.

final_claim: For the fixed-parameter equal-dwell switched planar system A0=[[0,-1],[1,a]], A1=[[-2d,-1],[1,a]], 0<a<2 and d>max(a,1/a), its stable dwell-time set has exactly one exponentially thin component near each late zero t_n=(arctan(eta)+pi/2+n*pi)/omega; endpoints t_n±exp(-sigma*t_n)/(omega*R)(1+o(1)), and exact geometric stable-tail measure constant 2/[omega*R*(1-exp(-sigma*pi/omega))]. Both frozen modes and their average are unstable, but the theorem does not claim stability of the full nonlinear Rössler system.
